name: CMOS Ring Oscillator — Odd-Stage Inverter Loop
description: Odd-stage feedback inverter chain. Oscillation frequency = 1/(2·N·t_pd) where N is stage count and t_pd is per-stage propagation delay.

High Speed.reasoning: Minimum L=0.15um and wide channels maximise frequency.

design_intents.decision_template: Odd-stage inverter loop with {stages} stages (W_P={w_p}um, W_N={w_n}um, L={l_val}um)
design_intents.reason: An odd number of inverting stages ensures the loop phase shift is exactly 360° (each inverter contributes 180°), which is the necessary condition for sustained oscillation. Even-stage loops have two stable states and latch up.
design_intents.tradeoffs: More stages reduce frequency but improve phase noise (jitter). Fewer stages maximise frequency but increase jitter.
references: CMOS VLSI Design - Weste & Harris Ch.11
Ring Oscillator Phase Noise - Hajimiri & Lee JSSC 1999

sizing_notes.M_P{i}: Inverter PMOS stage i — wider than NMOS to compensate lower hole mobility.
sizing_notes.M_N{i}: Inverter NMOS stage i — reference width; propagation delay is primarily determined by this device.
